anomalies.condition: Character_Definitions row 287 has Character_ID 'TIE_ADVANCED_x1'. gac.units enforces units_unit_id_format check (unit_id ~ '^[A-Z0-9]+(?:_[A-Z0-9]+)*$'), which the lowercase 'x1' segment fails.
anomalies.detail: Accepted by the owner on 2026-09-21. Character_ID TIE_ADVANCED_x1 is preserved byte-for-byte as the canonical unit_id and as the public characterDefinitions key; it is not renamed or normalised. The ARCH-105 units_unit_id_format constraint is corrected by an ordered follow-up migration that relaxes exactly one axis, letter case, and keeps every other structural rule: ASCII alphanumerics and underscores only, at least one character per segment, no leading or trailing underscore, and no consecutive underscores. TIE_ADVANCED_x1 is the only one of the 312 captured Character_ID values that relies on the newly allowed form; the other 311 also satisfy the original expression. The already-integrated ARCH-105 migration is unchanged, and the matching rollback refuses non-destructively if any stored unit relies on the widened form.
anomalies.source: ARCH-106 loader — conflict between the ARCH-103 baseline and the ARCH-105 schema

description: Deterministic migration decisions that transform the committed ARCH-103 baseline into the ARCH-105 canonical schema. Every anomaly recorded by the ARCH-103 capture report, and every additional conflict found by the ARCH-106 loader, has an explicit entry here. Three conditions that ARCH-106 initially reported as blockers were resolved by owner decision on 2026-09-21; two of those are implemented as ordered follow-up migrations that correct the ARCH-105 schema. The loader still refuses to write to a database while any entry has status BLOCKED, and only ever acts on a resolution it implements.

identityRules.attackArchetypeCode: archetype_code is the source Counter_ID, byte-for-byte.
identityRules.authority: Every migrated judgement is AUTHORED_BASELINE. The source carries no lock evidence, so no value is migrated as AUTHORED_LOCKED.
identityRules.battleType: An attack archetype is FLEET when any Counter_Composition member is a SHIP or CAPITAL_SHIP, otherwise SQUAD; the result is cross-checked against the modes the Counter_ID appears in on Counters and a disagreement is rejected. A defence-only archetype takes FLEET when every Counters mode it defends in is FLEET, SQUAD when none is, and is rejected when it spans both. A defence identity that never appears on Counters takes its battle type from its Defence_Teams mode, and is rejected when that mode is Any.
identityRules.defenceIdentityResolution: A defence display name reuses an attack archetype only when it matches exactly one team_archetypes.display_name. Zero matches create a defence-only archetype. Two or more matches are rejected as ambiguous. No fuzzy, case-insensitive or semantic matching is ever attempted.
identityRules.defenceOnlyCodeRule: DEF_ + the display name uppercased, with every character outside [A-Z0-9] replaced by _, runs of _ collapsed to one, and leading/trailing _ removed. On collision with an already-assigned archetype_code the loader appends _2, _3, ... taking the first free integer, processing names in ascending code-point order so the outcome is independent of source row order.
identityRules.leaderAndFlex: is_leader is false and flex_slots is 0 for every migrated profile. The source records neither, and ARCH-106 does not invent them.
identityRules.profiles: Squad attack compositions migrate once as mode ANY because they are currently shared across 3v3 and 5v5. Fleet attack compositions migrate as mode FLEET. Defence profiles are created only for the modes in which the identity actually appears, carry no members, and set members_complete = false.
identityRules.unitId: unit_id is the source Character_ID, byte-for-byte.

modeNormalisation.note: gac.catalogue_mode is an uppercase enum. Source spellings are normalised on the way in and projected back to their exact source spelling on the way out, per public domain. No public payload string changes.
